comments.author: JonnieCache
comments.story: Printers are spontaneously printing odd "SQL" strings
comments.why: Printer hacking talk showing firmware flaws in networked printers.
comments.text: Don't trust your printer! There were a lot of demos of printer hacks at 28c3 and basically I think I might not print anything ever again. A lot of these things have their firmware implemented in postscript. Updating the firmware consists of printing a special document. It's pretty mental tbh. Your jaw will be scraping along the floor at some of the holes these things have. Print Me If You Dare: [VIDEO] Hacking MFPs: [LINK] EDIT: Beaten by 4 hours. Oh well.

comments.story: HP printers can be remotely controlled and set on fire, researchers claim

comments.text: The disclosures before this talk gave rise to this article [VIDEO] The talk clearly mentions that if you can put malware into a printer wouldn't you use it to pawn a network instead of just setting it on fire - also it isn't possible to set it on fire - they just made that up.
